title: Collateral Advance Rate Schedule for Borrowing Base Lending — Operating Lines of Credit
content:
Credit administration publishes, for each of the Operating Lines of Credit, the advance rate the product lends at on each class of farm collateral reported on a borrowing base certificate.

## Collateral classes and their measure

| Class | Advance rate is a percentage of |
|---|---|
| Unpriced stored grain | market value |
| Stored grain under a priced contract | contract value |
| Feeder and slaughter livestock | market value |
| Eligible receivables | face value |
| Prepaid, unapplied crop inputs | invoiced cost |
| Insured growing crops | the insurance guarantee; this rate applies only under the crop insurance assignment rule |

## Product advance rates (percent)

| Product | Unpriced stored grain | Contracted grain | Market livestock | Receivables | Prepaid inputs | Insured growing crops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Revolving Operating Line | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | 75 | 85 | 75 | 80 | 70 | 65 |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | 80 | 90 | 75 | 85 | 70 | 60 |

## Points of reading

- Products that are not lent against a borrowing base carry a 0 rate in every class.
- On both borrowing base products, grain under a priced contract is lent against at a higher rate than unpriced grain, and insured growing crops at the lowest rate of the six classes.
- *Hypothetical illustration:* USD 100,000 of grain under a priced contract, stated on an Agribusiness Revolving Line certificate, corresponds to USD 90,000 at that product's 90% contracted grain rate.
